A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffAdapt and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original method and experiments can be matched reliably despite renumbering, relocation, and added analyses in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original entropy analyses, oracle experiments, benchmark evaluations, token savings, and latency measurements in Sections 3–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds probe and threshold ablations, heuristic and ThinkLess comparisons, and a reasoning-quality evaluation.

M1.justification: The labeling procedure, prefill hidden-state MLP, cross-entropy loss, and adaptive inference procedure remain unchanged. Prompts, default thresholds, temperatures, and token ratios match. The new 'Fail Fast' terminology redescribes the existing Hard strategy; no new termination rule or fallback implementation is specified.

E1.justification: Both use DeepMath-103K and the same eight evaluation benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME24/25, OlympiadBench, Minerva, GPQA, and MMLU-Pro. v3's cross-domain subsection reports additional detail for existing coverage. Its tuning, ThinkLess, and reasoning-quality studies reuse existing datasets and reasoning tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated ThinkLess Stage-2 RL comparator against DiffAdapt applied to Stage-1 Warmup in Table 10; v1 only discussed Thinkless in related work. Table 8 also introduces three uniform heuristic controls. The original fixed-strategy and DEER comparisons remain. Despite v3's prose, Table 10 does not separately report an unmodified Warmup baseline.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark settings are retained, but new studies introduce transferred thresholds, a linear-probe control, a 30% training subset, and ThinkLess Stage-1/Stage-2 model conditions. Appendix E adds a 50-question GSM8K sample and anonymized pairwise judging by Qwen3-30B-A3B for reasoning completeness, coherence, and conciseness. These are substantial additions to the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v3 adds threshold-transfer, probe-architecture, and training-data ablations in Section 7.1, and comparisons supporting strategy tuning in Appendix C.5. Section 7.2 and Appendix E add reasoning-integrity assessment and manual analysis of the six baseline-preferred cases, identifying one truncation error. These checks were absent from v1; the earlier entropy and oracle analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both specify ten samples per problem for entropy/labeling and three experimental runs with mean performance. v3 adds no actual seed values, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty-reporting procedure. Its generic statement about specifying seeds supplies no concrete seed information; the 50-query audit is an evaluation sample-size addition.

E6.justification: Matched original results remain unchanged, including 22.4% Qwen3-4B token savings and the 64/57/10-minute latency comparison. v3 adds ablation, tuning, MMLU-Pro, ThinkLess, and reasoning-quality results. For example, Table 10 reports 67.6% accuracy at 954 tokens for TL-Warmup plus DiffAdapt versus 63.3% at 1,460 tokens for TL-1.5B-RL on MATH500 at 50% budget. The audit reports 38/50 DiffAdapt preferences and one identified truncation error.

T1.justification: The entropy and correctness definitions, MLP and loss equations, token-savings formula, and labeling pseudocode are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. v3's additional grid-search selection description documents empirical tuning rather than new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: U-shaped entropy patterns, oracle potential, lightweight difficulty-based strategy selection without LLM retraining, compatibility with length-control RL, and up to 22.4% token savings across five models and eight benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets threshold transfer as supporting deployment without recalibration, reduced training data as demonstrating extreme data efficiency, and the judging study as refuting reasoning-integrity concerns and confirming fallback effectiveness. Appendix B adds a transferability qualification while retaining earlier limitations. Some interpretations exceed the evidence: the claimed minimal data-reduction impact includes a 6.7-point accuracy loss at full budget in Table 5.

D1.justification: v3 expands the previously mentioned grid search with 125 combinations, parameter ranges, and selection requiring at least 95% accuracy, and supplies the judging prompt and setup. A new reproducibility statement promises code, scripts, and configurations, without providing a new access link or actual seed values. Core implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including DAST, DLER, and work on LLM compression and serving, while preserving the related-work taxonomy and principal positioning. Appendix D.2 further contrasts DiffAdapt with ThinkLess's SFT-plus-RL requirements. Thinkless itself was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v3 adds an ablation section, appendix subsections, and reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements. It revises the Hard-strategy rationale and limitations, corrects some spelling, and changes the publication header. Most original scientific prose and the overall narrative remain intact; this is an extension rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the tabular presentation with ablation, judging/failure, tuning, MMLU-Pro, and ThinkLess displays. Existing plots and the framework diagram are unchanged, while efficiency tables are arranged side by side and the oracle summary is relocated. Original Figures 2–3 become Tables 1–2, leaving the oracle plot labeled as a table and its Section 4 Figure 2 reference pointing to the framework diagram.

improvement.justification: v3 makes previously untested design choices more assessable through ablations, a direct ThinkLess comparison, and clearer tuning and judging procedures. These provide useful validation beyond v1. The gain is limited by reporting and interpretation problems: Table 5's averages do not match the arithmetic means of its displayed rows, its reduced-data condition loses 6.7 points at full budget despite claims of minimal degradation, and the 50-query audit supports a narrower conclusion than refuting reasoning-integrity concerns. The added evidence improves the paper, but these weaknesses prevent a substantial overall improvement.
